pinboard.title: Watched · Something watched you this week
Jensen Huang said to have had relationship with Nvidia executive who reports to him • The New York Times
pinboard.description:
Ryan Mac, Tripp Mickle and Georgia Gee:

Jensen Huang, the leader of Nvidia who is under investigation for an affair with a woman who US intelligence determined is a Chinese spy, also had an extramarital relationship with an executive who reports to him, according to five people who worked at the company. The relationship, which has not been previously reported, was with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of health care, said the people, who spoke under the condition of anonymity to describe sensitive information. Under Nvidia’s code of conduct, employees are told to “avoid situations where our actions create conflict” including “personal relationships,” and the company states that it “promptly investigates reports of misconduct.” Many corporations have policies against managers having relationships with subordinates. Mr. Huang, 63, and Ms. Powell, 48, were captured on video being affectionate at a San Jose, Calif., hotel during a Nvidia conference in March, according to two of the people who worked at the company. The New York Times has not seen the video. Both Mr. Huang and Ms. Powell are married to other people.

The NY Times is going to pick away at this story endlessly, because it knows there's a goldmine. Meanwhile, Nvidia starts to look less like a well-run company and more like one guy's personal fiefdom. (The WSJ suggests that the board will try to force him out.)

pinboard.title: How a Misquote by a Supreme Court Justice Imperils Gun Restrictions - The New York Times
pinboard.description:
Saul Cornell, a Second Amendment scholar and history professor at Fordham University, said relying on centuries-old legal precedents requires understanding how earlier generations used language. He said “dangerous and unusual” is most likely an example of hendiadys, in which a single concept is expressed in multiple words connected by “and.” One famous example of hendiadys is Shakespeare’s “full of sound and fury,” which meant furious sound.

“The best translation of Blackstone’s terminology,” Dr. Cornell said, “would be to treat ‘dangerous and unusual’ as a synonym for unusually dangerous.”

pinboard.title: ‘Ahead of his time’: AI helps unlock discoveries hidden in notebooks of man who transformed maths | Mathematics | The Guardian
pinboard.description:
The first task von Plato set Claude was to discover if Gödel’s workbooks had a proof of the independence of the axiom of choice, which would reveal that Gödel had been telling the truth in 1966. The answer came back: yes, almost. “He was just one step away,” said von Plato. “There’s one definition that Gödel got wrong, but he had the right definition two years earlier, and so the thought is that he would have arrived at the right definition anyway if he had just continued for a few months. For me, the architecture of his proof is just wonderful. It makes all of these results of set theory follow a uniform pattern.

“What strikes me especially is that he starts from ideas. He’s not like someone who plays with formulas and hopes to arrive somewhere. He has very, very clear ideas, and then he’s methodical. Step after step he goes ahead and he manages to fulfil the aims that he has in this formal work.”
